# RS2 v2.0 FULL EQUITY ANALYSIS — ResMed Inc. (RMD)

**To the reviewer:** The following is my complete analysis, SECTION 0–SECTION 12. I executed web research first — before building any forecast — to ground FY2027 guidance, capex plans, the Astral/MatrixCare/Noctrix portfolio math, and current macro inputs. All retrieved figures are cited inline; everything I could not establish is marked [Unconfirmed] and carried into the scenario range rather than buried in a point estimate. The valuation is built from the filed fiscal-year series (FY2026 base), not from the withheld TTM.

---

## SECTION 0 — HOW TO READ THIS ANALYSIS

**Scope and sourcing conventions.** This is an RS2 v2.0 equity analysis of ResMed Inc. The data pack (SECTION 1–12) supplies the SEC-filed historical series. I supplemented it with web research during my reasoning — before concluding — for precisely the things filings cannot tell me: forward guidance, capex plans, portfolio transactions, and the discount-rate environment.

| Label | Meaning |

| [Filed] | SEC XBRL as held in the pack |
| [Arithmetic] | Exact arithmetic on filed values |
| [Actual] | Management/company or regulator statement retrieved this session |
| [Estimate] | Secondary source (newspaper, blog, transcript aggregator) |
| [Assumption] | My own judgment — always disclosed |
| [Unconfirmed] | Could not be verified; carried into scenarios |

**Key research findings that frame everything below:**

1. **FY2027 formal guidance (first-ever issued):** revenue **$5.75B–$5.85B**, non-GAAP EPS **$12.00–$12.25**, capex **$160M–$180M**, buyback **$1.5B** (incl. $450M ASR), dividend +10% to $0.66/qtr. [[Actual] — Investing.com transcript of Q4 FY2026 earnings call, Aug 6, 2026](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-resmed-beats-eps-in-q4-2026-but-shares-fall-after-hours-93CH-4844625). This guidance is the single most important forward input — ResMed never issued annual guidance before.
2. **FY2026 non-GAAP EPS: $11.17** [[Estimate] — Motley Fool, Aug 7, 2026](https://www.fool.com.au/2026/08/07/resmed-posts-strong-q4-earnings-lifts-dividend/). Midpoint guidance implies +8.6% EPS growth on +2.6% headline revenue growth — the difference is portfolio mix and buybacks.
3. **Portfolio math behind the low headline growth:** MatrixCare divested (~$220M FY26 revenue, ~$55M op profit — [[Estimate] MedTechDive](https://www.medtechdive.com/news/resmed-to-sell-matrixcare-for-490m-to-private-equity-firm/824709/)); Noctrix acquired (+$30M FY27 revenue, −$0.20 EPS — [[Estimate] kosec.com.au](https://kosec.com.au/resmed-sells-matrixcare-for-us490-million/)); Astral ventilator suspension (−$75M FY27 revenue, −$0.15 EPS, $42M provision — [[Estimate] Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4628719-resmed-expects-fy-2027-revenue-of-5_75b-5_85b-and-non-gaap-eps-of-12-12_25-while-accelerating) / [Actual] transcript).
4. **Underlying core growth ex-portfolio:** management guided core constant-currency growth **5–7%** ex MatrixCare/Noctrix; **6–8%** after backing out Astral. I verified this arithmetic internally (Section 10).
5. **Macro inputs:** 10-yr UST ≈ **4.69%** (Aug 20, 2026 — [Actual] US Treasury via TradingEconomics/calcfi); implied ERP ≈ **4.28%** (Damodaran, Aug 1, 2026 — [Estimate]).
6. **Unresolved data issues (carried forward, not hidden):**
   - The pack's filed capex ($0.156B FY2026, PP&E only) **excludes capitalized software**; the vendor's capex ($0.101B) is lower still; management's guided $160–180M is broader. **I use management's guided total for FY2027 and scale it thereafter** — the exact software/PP&E split is [Unconfirmed].
   - The pack's `change in WC` column **includes cash** and is therefore not an operating-WC measure; I model operating WC as ~neutral (Section 11).
   - The $260M FY2026 "current portion" equal to "short-term borrowings" suggests one instrument mapped twice; I treat them as one debt item (Section 6).

## SECTION 1 — IDENTITY & BUSINESS

**Ticker:** RMD · **Sector:** Healthcare · **Industry:** Medical Instruments & Supplies · **Fiscal year end:** June 30 [Actual — management: "We closed out another great fiscal year for ResMed on June 30th", Q4 FY2026 call]. **Newest held quarter in pack:** 2026-03-31 (Q3 FY2026); the June-2026 quarter exists in the annual FY2026 line but not as a quarterly row (Section 3 derives it as a residual).

**Business.** ResMed is a two-player-dominant supplier of sleep-disordered-breathing (SDB) therapy — CPAP devices, masks, and respiratory care — plus connected-care software (Brightree, MEDIFOX DAN, AirView). The economics are attractive: recurring mask/consumable revenue, a low-beta demand base (OSA is under-diagnosed globally), a 25% ROE, and 100%+ FCF conversion.

**FY2026 business portfolio events (all sourced in Section 0):** MatrixCare divestiture **completed** (sold to Frazier Healthcare for ~$490M); Noctrix Health (hypoglossal-nerve-stimulation adjunct) acquired for $340M; Astral ventilator field-safety action taken ($42M provision, −$75M FY27 revenue); first-ever formal FY guidance issued; dividend raised 10%.

**Competitive position (from research brief [Estimate]):** Dominant share in CPAP masks/devices; entrenched via connected-care data; Philips re-entering could pressure share; GLP-1 drugs are a structural demand question for OSA device therapy; wearable partnerships (ŌURA) are a demand-creation funnel — management reports 13,000 users referred and "75% previously undiagnosed" [Actual, prepared remarks]. The moat is real but being tested on three fronts (Philips, GLP-1, patent IPR IPR2026-00341).

**What the pack does NOT hold — and why it matters:** zero dimensional/segment XBRL tags (no sum-of-the-parts possible); no marketable-securities line (cash may be understated); no effective tax rate (I assume 20%, Section 11); no analyst Q&A (Section 10 contains prepared remarks only).

**Guidance arithmetic (my verification, [Arithmetic] on retrieved figures):**

- FY2026 revenue $5.653B **[Filed]** includes MatrixCare ~$0.220B **[Estimate]**. FY2027 base ex-MatrixCare ≈ $5.433B.
- Add Noctrix +$0.030B **[Estimate]**; back out Astral −$0.075B **[Estimate]**.
- Midpoint revenue $5.800B ⇒ implied organic core growth = (5.800 + 0.075 − 0.030) / 5.433 − 1 = **+7.6%**. Low end ⇒ **+6.7%**.

**Conclusion:** the guidance is internally coherent. Reported FY2027 growth of +2.6% headline is a mirage — the underlying core business is growing 6.7–7.6%, in the middle of management's stated 6–8%. The £0.265B of reported-mix drag (MatrixCare −$220M, Noctrix +$30M, Astral −$75M) explains the gap. EPS guidance of +8.6% at midpoint is consistent with that core growth plus ~4% share-count reduction from buybacks, partially offset by the ~$0.35 combined EPS drag of Astral and Noctrix dilution (which management references: $0.15 + $0.20).

**What this means for the forecast beyond FY2027:** management's five-year model is "high single-digit revenue growth, earnings growth outpaces revenue" [Estimate — Motley Fool summary of prior statements]. Post-FY2027, the recurring base is the 6–8% core business with a clean mix. **This is a guided near-term path and an anchored long-term model — the years in between are my interpolation, explicitly labelled as such in Section 11.**
